doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Cannonball Adderley at Cafe Bohemia and musicians recommending each other
summary: He played a month with Cannonball and recommended Sam Jones; they discuss Blakey and Hampton finding replacements.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: You worked with one of my favorite people of all time, Cannonball Adderley.

I met him in New York and we became friends or something. And I left Dinah at one time, and he was going into the Cafe Bohemia, and he said, “well come on in, I’m going in for a month.” And I said okay. And I went in for a month with him and it was Cannon, Nat, Junior Mance and Specks Wright out of Philadelphia, and myself. And then I went back to Washington, I had to go back to Washington, and so he said, “well can you recommend a bass player?” And I said well a good friend of mine is Sam Jones, try and get him, he’s very good. And he got Sam and then Cannon started going right up the ladder, yeah.
I think it’s really fascinating how musicians recommend each other and they move around from group to group.
Well you notice with Art Blakey’s group that anybody was leaving, he’d tell them, “you get me somebody that’s like you.”
That’s how that worked. He wound up getting young, good guys, and he would tell them, “if you’re leaving, get someone.” And Lionel Hampton would just go out and find them.
